newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - FORMER RAMS CORNERBACK SENTENCED TO 40 YEARS IN JAIL.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - FORMER RAMS CORNERBACK SENTENCED TO 40 YEARS IN JAIL.

text.p: Former National Football League star Darryl Henley was sentenced on Monday to more than 40 years in prison for drug trafficking and conspiracy to murder a judge and the cheerleader who testified against him.
Henley, a former cornerback for the Los Angeles Rams, was sentenced by two federal judges in Los Angeles after pleading guilty to conspiracy to murder and being found guilty of drug trafficking.

Prosecutors said Henley's targets in the murder-for-hire scheme were ex-Rams cheerleader Tracy Donaho, who testified in the drug trafficking trial that she had transported cocaine across the country for him, and U.S. District Judge Gary Taylor, who presided over that trial.
According to prosecutors, Henley conspired to have the two murdered while he was in jail. But the killings never occurred.
U.S. District Court Judge Manual Real sentenced Henley to 260 months -- just over 21 1/2 years -- in jail on the drug charges, telling him, "You really screwed up your life, didn't you."

In another court, Federal Judge James Ideman sentenced Henley, 30, to 235 months -- or just over 19 1/2 years -- on the murder conspiracy charges, recommending that he serve his time in the U.S. penitentiary in Marion, Illinois, one of the nation's highest security facilities.
"If ever there was a guy who needs to be locked down 24 hours a day it's Henley," Ideman said.
